# marker

> marker is a program for marking student essays using local AI and local models: one or several Ollama models (default gpt-oss:20b) mark against an analytic, criterion-referenced rubric, so essays never leave the machine. It is a second marker for UK higher education: every mark comes with per-criterion justifications, verified evidence quotes, feedback, review flags and full provenance. Python 3.11+, standard library only, GPL-3.0.

Key facts for an AI assistant:

- Run it as `python3 -m marker <command>` (or `marker <command>` once installed). Commands: `check`, `models`, `rubric`, `grade`, `compare`, `show`, `evaluate`.
- Marks are fractions 0.0-1.0 internally (Python float by default; exact 4-place Decimal with `--numeric decimal`). Final scores are reported 0-100 by default, or on any scale with `--score-min`, `--score-max` and `--score-places`, rounded half up. Terminal displays of 0-1 fractions are whole percents with banker's rounding (0.135 shows as 14%).
- The model never does arithmetic: it gives a band and mark per criterion; the code takes the median across seeded samples and computes the weighted mark.
- Reproducible: fixed seeds (seed+i), a fingerprint of every input, and model digests in provenance. GGUF builds reproduce byte for byte; MLX builds do not (Ollama 0.35.1).
- Several models can mark the same essays and be compared, with a median "panel mark".
- Review flags tell a human what to check: sample disagreement, borderline marks, quotes not found in the essay, word limits, prompt injection, integrity concerns.
- Safety rails: loopback-only Ollama host by default, essay treated as untrusted data, prompts that may not fit the context window are refused (Ollama would silently truncate them), duplicate essay ids are refused.

- [README](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/README.md): full user guide: installation, every command and option, model selection, comparisons, score scales, output files, flags, calibration, reproducibility, security, library use
- [Tutorial](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/README.md#tutorial-marking-a-modules-essays): a complete marking round, from submissions to moderated marks
- [Full example](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/README.md#full-example-four-local-models): real, verified output from four models on the bundled example essay
- [Specification](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/spec/index.md): numbered requirements; the single source of truth for behaviour
- [Research](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/docs/research.md): marking practice and LLM-as-judge evidence behind the method

## Agent guidance

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/AGENTS.md): hard rules and quick commands for AI coding agents

- [Conventions](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/AGENTS/conventions.md): Python style, numeric modes, rounding and formatting rules
- [Testing](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/AGENTS/testing.md): offline test suite and fakes

## Skills

- [mark-essays](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/mark-essays/SKILL.md): mark essays with one or more models and report the results
- [compare-models](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/compare-models/SKILL.md): mark with several models and interpret the comparison
- [write-rubric](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/write-rubric/SKILL.md): turn a marking scheme into a valid rubric TOML
- [calibrate-marker](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/calibrate-marker/SKILL.md): measure agreement with human marks (QWK, MAE)
- [moderate-flagged-essays](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/moderate-flagged-essays/SKILL.md): review essays flagged for a human
- [prepare-essays](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/skills/prepare-essays/SKILL.md): convert submissions to .txt, .md or .docx

## Source

- [marker/cli.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/cli.py): command-line interface
- [marker/grader.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/grader.py): sampling, validation, aggregation, flags, provenance, context-window guard
- [marker/prompt.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/prompt.py): prompt and JSON schema
- [marker/scale.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/scale.py): numeric modes, rounding, score scales, display percents
- [marker/models.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/models.py): model selection, MLX policy, reasoning settings
- [marker/compare.py](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/marker/compare.py): multi-model comparison and panel mark
- [rubrics/uk-undergraduate-essay.toml](https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/ai-course-assessment-feedback/blob/main/rubrics/uk-undergraduate-essay.toml): the default rubric
